items.name: ExpressionDepthChecker
items.summary: An expression "transform" that doesn't actually change the expression at all. Instead, it measures the maximum depth of a expression, with a depth limit to prevent stack overflow. Useful for verifying that a expression has reasonable depth…

methods.name: check_expr
methods.signature: fn check_expr(expr: &Expression, depth_limit: usize) -> usize
methods.summary: Depth-checks the given expression against a given depth limit. The return value is the largest depth seen, which is capped at one more than the depth limit (indicating the recursion was terminated).

methods.name: check_pred
methods.signature: fn check_pred(pred: &Predicate, depth_limit: usize) -> usize
methods.summary: Depth-checks the given predicate against a given depth limit. The return value is the largest depth seen, which is capped at one more than the depth limit (indicating the recursion was terminated).

methods.name: transform_expr
methods.signature: fn transform_expr(&mut self, expr: &'a Expression) -> Self::Output<Expression>
methods.summary: General entry point for transforming an expression. This method will dispatch to the specific transform for each expression variant. Also invoked internally in order to recurse on the child(ren) of non-leaf expressions.

methods.summary: Called for each binary expression encountered during the traversal. The provided implementation just forwards to [`Self::recurse_into_expr_binary`].
